October, 1991 Page Reply How to write to us...02 - Ted Payne............03 07 Billy Humphries......08 10 Brian Cooper.........13 15 John Hall............16 17 John White...........19 22 Charlie Kingwell.....23 28 Chris Oliver.........34 36 PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated! Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address. From: Ted Payne, SOUTHPORT Dear Ron & Brian, My equipment is now as follows, Spectrum +3,Multiface 3 and Star LC10 viewed through a Samsung 14" colour portable. Before I got the printer I had noted with interest the letters in OUTLET and in some paper mag- azines about the many and varied problems that people had getting different things to work. However, unless my particular +3 is unique (I doubt it) I don't understand why, because everything in OUTLET I want to print out I just press the relevant key(s) and the Star bursts into life and I get perfect hard copy.Even Tasword 2 (the disc version you published a while back) prints perfectly as the hard copy of this letter proves. I've read a couple of letters from people who seem to be having problems feeding a signal from a Spectrum into a video. The main problem I came across when I tried it was that the frequency used to send the signal from the video to the TV is almost the same as the signal from a Spectrum. If you use a T aerial connector in the back of your TV and feed both a video and a speccy in then the picture for either is distorted. The solution is to put the T connector into the VIDEO aerial IN socket then plug the leads from the Speccy and the aerial into it. If your video has one, select the test mode. (usually a switch at the back) Find a small hole at the back of the video through which you can see a small screw head. Sometimes it is marked UHF or with some numbers e.g., 38-62. Turn this screw to the left or right about a quarter of an inch. All you are doing is adjusting the frequency of the signal from the video to the TV.Then re-tune the video channel on your TV until you get the picture from the video. Once you have the video picture on your TV the only thing left to do is switch off the test mode (if you had one) then tune a spare channel on the video until you get the Speccy screen on the TV. Hey Presto! Now you can record anything you do on the Speccy for hours of action replays or you could record your favourite bits of OUTLET to look at even without a Speccy in the same house. By the way, can you recommend a good, easy-to-use and cheap,desk top publishing program for a +3? Thanks for taking the trouble to produce such a great magazine, Best regards, Ted Payne Brian Cavers to Ted Payne Thanks, Ted. There is really only one desktop publishing program for the Spec- trum: P.C.G.'s DTP PACK. This is three programs: WORDMASTER, the wordprocessor:`13.95, HEADLINER, graphic/title designer: `10.95 and TYPELINER,the actual desktop publisher:`18.95. All three programs are integrated so the main program accesses the others easily from disc. The complete pack is `37.95. These prices are for tape or Disciple/+D disc.Add `2 for the +3 disc version.Write P.C.G., 61 School Street,Barrow- in-Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW (Tel:0229 836957) - Brian From: Billy Humphries Firstly, I would like to say how much I enjoy your magazine - you put in so much every month. I need information regarding printers. I have a 128 Spectrum, (black) a 48+, and a DISCIPLE. I want to buy a 24-pin colour printer to do screen dumps of pictures, listings and hard copies of video lists etc. I buy OUTLET on tape and copy it to drive with RUN 9982. I would like to copy textfiles but so far the only success is when I copy the text loader,(any one) break when the play tape prompt is on and LOAD the code of the text file from the disc that has been SAVEd by using'Oli's Readr' (OUTLET 14) to find the address and length and copying the code LOAD 'NAME' CODE ADD,LEN. Is there a better, neater way? You could possibly tell me a quick way to LOAD all the text files on one disc and then a program could be used like PROMPT load code from tape; (y/n?) SAVE code to disc, print to screen to printer, LOAD next file from tape/disc. I look forward to the next issue and hope you can help with the printer. Thanks, Billy Humphries Brian Cavers to Billy Humphries I'd go for the Citizen Swift 24 which has an optional "colour kit" It's priced between `300 to `400 but if I were you I'd shop around to get the best price and try to get a shop demo. I listed a bit of info about it in my reply to Norman Haigh in OUTLETTERS 45 but a full review by Mike Pike was in Issue 48 if you have that issue. However, note that I have not used the machine personally but on paper it looks excellent and has had good reviews. I would recommend you try PBT. They sell the SWIFT 24 at only `295.50+`5 pp. and they can also sell you the colour ribbons at `14.99 PBT are at Port Talbot Workshops Unit 17, Addison Road, Port Talbot,SA12 6HZ. Tel:0639 885008 They do +D and Disciple repairs too so are au fait with the Spectrum. I can recommend them. Incidentally, to get colour screen dumps you would need some special software. If you do try PBT you might ask them. I know they have some colour dump soft- ware but it may be 9-pin only and it may be for SAM only. I just forget now. I think it's the one written by Darren Talbot that we had in OUTBOARD some time ago. Sorry, I can't just pin it down at the moment and I have a memory like a (what do they call those things that are full of holes?). Regarding transferring OUTLET files from tape to +D disc, the easiest way is to use UNITRANS+ (OUTLET 20).This is an excellent program and does the job fully automatically. However,note that it doesn't change BASIC so any that loads other files will need syntax changing etc. Now that you will have seen our new prices I'm sure you will have realized there is no point in getting the tape version any more if you have a +D as they are the same price! - Brian From Brian Cooper Dear Ron And Brian, Thank you for another super 'Outlet'. I wonder if you can help me with the following problem arising from the excellent 'Card Index' program (OUTLET 48) from Stuart Redfern and his Dad! (Nothing wrong with the program - just my lack of know-how)? I'm unable to get my printer, a CPA.80+, to do a linefeed when printing out the index card information. Stuart and his Dad advise alteration of line 7000 but as I say, my programming knowledge is rather limited. The line reads as follows: 7000 POKE @VAL"6",NOT PI: RETURN Many thanks for your help and keep up the good work! - Brian Cooper PS. Could you please pass on my grateful thanks to the person from Wiltshire who very kindly answered my plea for a 'TLW' manual. I don't know your name or address but thank you. Thanks also to the other Spectrum fans who offered help! Brian Cavers to Brian Cooper Yes, the answer is to alter line 355 as follows:LIST the line and insert an apostrophe between the word LPRINT and m$(n) near the end of the line thus changing... LPRINT m$(n) to LPRINT'm$(n) The BASIC apostrophe in a PRINT or LPRINT statement (NOT within quotation marks) causes a line feed so LPRINT''''' would do 5 linefeeds. Incidentally, putting POKE @6,1:LPRINT CHR$27;"W";CHR$ 1: at the start of line 7000 gives wide print. +3 users replace POKE @6,1 with FORMAT LPRINT "U".Microdrive and Opus use OPEN #3;"B": - Brian From: John Hall, BOURNEMOUTH I receive OUTLET on 3.5" disks for use with the Plus D system, and all is well until you put programs like the German Folk Song on the disk. My Plus D is used with a Spectrum +3 which, of course, I cannot use in the 128K mode. Can I convert the program from my disk to run in 128k mode or do I have to order a Plus 3 disk? I very much appreciate the quality and variety of the programs which I have received so far. Have any of your earlier disks included any fractal programs? John Hall Brian Cavers to John Hall I'm told you can't get into the 128K BASIC editor if the +D is attached to the +3 so, load the program from +D, BREAK, enter: 8917 IF K$="S" THEN GO TO 9972 RUN 9983 to SAVE to tape. Reset to get the 128K menu loader and re-load from tape by pressing ENTER with no disc in the +3 drive and it should run O.K. You may be able to do a 48K or 128K snapshot to the +D drive or, if you press "S" at the title page, it should save to +3 disc and should reload as a boot file at the loader menu.I can't test any of this of course! There's an excellent fractal program by Chris and Paul Oliver in OUTLET 35 called BROT. The Spectrum obviously can't compete with the Amiga's graphics and processing speed capability but BROT is, nevertheless, able to produce some good Mandelbrot images.Other fractal programs of interest are TRI2 (OUTLET 34)and FRAX (OUTLET 16).Another program you may enjoy which involves entering values to produce great 3D images (but which is NOT a fractal generator) is ISOMETRIC (OUTLET 26). I reckon it's a terrific program. - Brian From: John White, LEICESTER Dear Ron & Brian, Thank you for another quality OUTLET (Issue 048). With reference to John Couch's letter about printing the "`" sign on the Citizen 120-D+ and Brian's reply, I used to have my 120-D set for the English characters when I used Tasword 2 but have now reset it for "#=#" and altered the T2 printer codes to put those quoted by Brian on to Key 8 in Graphics mode. I can now bring in the English characters if I want the ` in text. Having said that, I now normally use Tasword 3 and if John Couch (or others) do also, it should be possible for them to print `#`#`#`#`#`#`# to their hearts' content! I don't know what the D+ has that my D hasn't but my method is:- 1. Go to TW3 menu and select C to customise the program. 2. Keep pressing ENTER until "define normal print chars". 3. Answer Y and follow prompts. Type in "`" and enter 27 94 156 and ENTER again to leave the sequence. 4. If no keys have been defined to select IBM and Epson modes then:- 5. Answer Y to "define printer control chars" and press space for the other 16 chars. 6. Choose a key for IBM mode and enter 27 126 53 49. 7. Choose a key for Epson mode and enter 27 126 53 48. 8. Press ENTER when finished and hold until the menu returns. 9. Re-SAVE the program with T to make this permanent. The "`" sign is in the printer's IBM alternative character set and so IBM mode must be selected at any convenient point before the first "`" is typed (bearing in mind that the codes for some other functions may be different in IBM mode) and Epson restored after the last one. (For example CHR$ 27;"G"/ CHR$ 27;"H" will set/cancel double strike in Epson and CQ (NLQ) in IBM modes) Incidentally, I can report that since I fitted the gold-plated plug to my Spectrum 48K over 12 months ago I've had no crashes! Best wishes to you both, John H.B. White Thanks, John. - Brian From: Charlie Kingwell, OAKHAM [SUBJECT:BOTH SAM AND SPECTRUM!] I hadn't realised before just how versatile CATLOADER is (OUTLET 33) - it certainly transforms SAM! Having purposely got a twin- drive machine to make things easy then finding Samdos2 didn't seem to understand about two drives, I'd given up trying to do anything useful with it. NOT ANY MORE! Now I've found I can transfer text files from Spectrum to SAM easily.CATLOADER makes it simple to sort out file transfer between Tasword discs. I have a problem, however. I used the 'Opus to SAM converter program' (SAM Supp.2 program 3.P) for the SAM to read a 512 sector Opus disc. I found that it would transfer 1 or 2 files and then crash - eventually I put it down to a bad disc. (Incidentally, have you come across a 'disc check' program that writes/reads all tracks?) Having got a better disc, I then found that it wouldn't work properly in Drive 2. It stops with the message: 23 Invalid colour 90:2, line 90 being 90 LET disc$=cat$(7 TO 16):PRINT "Discname:<";disc$;">" Any comments? I was amazed at the difference that the 'Cinemascope' SAM screen makes to the presentation of OUTLET, it's just so pretty! It was always a pleasure to read OUTLET - now I can appreciate your artistry on each page too. I hadn't appreciated just how much you had hidden in the 'Add- Enders' until I read the letters and found answers to questions that had bothered me for some time.Of course,this was balanced by the generation of more puzzles! Yes, I'll be glad to take up your offer to have the SAM version of OUTLET instead of Opus and thus have another subject for experiment with MESSENGER - putting OUTLET on an 80-track Opus disk - providing MESSENGER will do this. As I've just got into this Micronet lark, more bits of jargon have appeared. What is "scrolling software" and what is it used for? Could someone tell us all about the various types of code files that seem to be in use.What uses what and why? By this I mean text, data, open-type, ASCII, array, etc. If I do a CAT*1 on the Opus in the vicinity of Masterfile I get file types of for Basic and for Code- I suppose f$() might be Data but what is

? I found out by accident that Tasword 2 text files LOAD at 32000 on the Spectrum (and 97536 on the SAM?) but never seen this in writing. Sometimes there are queries about the ROM in the Opus Discovery regarding disassembly, etc. As Paul Cheffings has produced a new version of the ROM (EXCOM) no doubt he could supply all ROM details required. Ring him on 0507 - 328794. I've just had several 'verify failed' messages- can't find an edge connector to clean, what next? Just copied "Tasword" onto this disc in Drive 2. Then went to LOAD this file from it- it went back to Drive 1! Charlie Kingwell Brian Cavers to Charlie Kingwell Yes, CATLOADER is one of several of our programs that, if we had put it in a glossy package and charged `9.99 both Spectrum and SAM users would have been there queuing at the door!Give it away in OUTLET and many do not really appreciate what they've got.That said, I must admit that it needs updating - especially for use with Masterdos and I have a lot of notes for improvements. What I don't have is time - as usual! Brian Gaff's AUTOMENU(OUTLET 34) will check and verify all tracks and sectors on a SAM disc or SEEK 'N PEEK(OUTLET 45) will display and edit sectors. Regarding SAM SUPPLEMENT's own program to read an Opus disc I can only recommend you write to them! After all, the original author of the program should be able to help better than I. The error appears to be that it is trying to print the name of the Opus disc from the CAT sector in DISC$ but it contains a code of between 16 to 21(PAPER,INK,etc.) followed by a value that is too high (e.g., INK 99!). This could mean you named the disc with a funny name (e.g. CHR$ 17+CHR$ 99 +"TEE HEE!") but is more likely that the program is looking at the wrong sector or the wrong part of the sector. The drive number should not matter but, as I say, I'm sure SAM SUPPLEMENT will try to help. MICRONET has VIEWDATA pages that are screens displayed one at a time then cleared and the next screen displayed. Many (most?) other bulletin boards display text but when the screen is full and more text is added the early text is just scrolled up off the top of the screen just as when you keep using a BASIC PRINT statement on SAM or Spectrum. It needs special software to access these bulletin boards called "Scrolling software". DR.SCROLL,`5-from B.G. SERVICES, 64 Roebuck Road, Chessington, Surrey, KT9 1JX works with the VTX5000 to let you access these "scrolling boards". B.G. also do a `1 PD tape with bits including scrolling software. 'P' in a CAT display is probably a 'PRINT' or 'OPEN-TYPE' file (these are synonymous terms). It can be "written" or PRINTed to just like printing to the screen or a printer and "read" with the use of INPUT or INKEY$. Consult your Opus or Masterdos manual! A text file is not a special disc file but any file (BASIC, CODE, OPEN-TYPE) containing text and, perhaps, print codes.ASCII files are virtually synonymous. In the case of Tasword 2 it is CODE but on many computers, OPEN-TYPE files are more commonly used for text. Likewise 'data' could be any values in BASIC or CODE etc. used by a program. However, on SAM and Spectrum, DATA files are BASIC arrays which have been saved (again, see your manual!). The "VERIFY FAILED" message I assume is in Tasword 2 on the SAM, yes? If so, it is almost certain that you are using an early version of MASTERDOS that has a bug. Apply for an upgrade or remove the VERIFY command from the BASIC in Tasword. Wait until it crashes again then note down the line number.We had this in OUTLET recently but I forget the line number. As for Tasword reverting to Drive 1, remove your disc, try again, wait a few seconds for it to crash, note the line number and adjust the load command. Why not add an INPUT? For example, INPUT "Enter drive No.";DN$ then make the load command... LOAD "D"+DN$+":"+N$. The 'N$' at the end must be whatever string name is used in your Tasword already.I think the version you have uses A$ and if you can see DEVICE D1 in lines 2020 and 2040 then remove them instead of the foregoing and you should then find you will access the "current drive". If you want to be able to change the drive number though,try the preceding. Ah, yes, I think the VERIFY in your version is at the end of line 1040. Just press B at the main Tasword menu to enter BASIC and after making the changes enter RS to resave the program. Hope that helps. - Brian. From: Chris Oliver, STAFFS Dear Brian & Ron, Enclosed is my contribution to the OUTLET `5000 fund with fervent wishes that you are able to keep on producing the superb mag. for many more than just another 12 months. To add my views to recent comments on the amount of Sam space:- Yes, it is a little disappointing that the content is no longer totally for the 48K machines but there are so many other good bits in every issue that you shouldn't consider this a real complaint. I often wonder though, what musical treats the 128ers get that we don't? Talking of music: an IBM- compatible has infiltrated our household(purely for educational purposes,of course) but who said they're not games machines? If you can, look at a game called "Wing Commander". To appreciate it fully you'll need a midi interface to a stereo sound system. It's compressed on five discs so you will also need two megabytes to expand into. The involvement is so great that it feels natural between missions to go into the on-screen bar, have a chat to the barman and relax by playing a video-game version of "Wing Commander". I can't remember who it was in the 1960s who couldn't envisage home computers needing any more than 1k of RAM? It's encouraging to see from the letters that you are getting new readers, but I suppose they've all got Super SAMS? Congratulations on the continu- ing high standards of OUTLET and best wishes for the future. Cheers, Chris Oliver Thanks Chris. For anyone who may be wondering what the `5000 fund is - it was just a joke about us ruefully pondering the amount of payments we've paid out over the years for all the programs contributed to OUTLET! - Brian.

(For example CHR$ 27;"G"/ CHR$ 27;"H" will set/cancel double strike in Epson and CQ (NLQ) in IBM modes) Incidentally, I can report that since I fitted the gold-plated plug to my Spectrum 48K over 12 months ago I've had no crashes! Best wishes to you both, John H.B. White Thanks, John. - Brian From: Charlie Kingwell, OAKHAM [SUBJECT:BOTH SAM AND SPECTRUM!] I hadn't realised before just how versatile CATLOADER is (OUTLET 33) - it certainly transforms SAM! Having purposely got a twin- drive machine to make things easy then finding Samdos2 didn't seem to understand about two drives, I'd given up trying to do anything useful with it. NOT ANY MORE! Now I've found I can transfer text files from Spectrum to SAM easily.CATLOADER makes it simple to sort out file transfer between Tasword discs. I have a problem, however. I used the 'Opus to SAM converter program' (SAM Supp.2 program 3.P) for the SAM to read a 512 sector Opus disc. I found that it would transfer 1 or 2 files and then crash - eventually I put it down to a bad disc. (Incidentally, have you come across a 'disc check' program that writes/reads all tracks?) Having got a better disc, I then found that it wouldn't work properly in Drive 2. It stops with the message: 23 Invalid colour 90:2, line 90 being 90 LET disc$=cat$(7 TO 16):PRINT "Discname:<";disc$;">" Any comments? I was amazed at the difference that the 'Cinemascope' SAM screen makes to the presentation of OUTLET, it's just so pretty! It was always a pleasure to read OUTLET - now I can appreciate your artistry on each page too. I hadn't appreciated just how much you had hidden in the 'Add- Enders' until I read the letters and found answers to questions that had bothered me for some time.Of course,this was balanced by the generation of more puzzles! Yes, I'll be glad to take up your offer to have the SAM version of OUTLET instead of Opus and thus have another subject for experiment with MESSENGER - putting OUTLET on an 80-track Opus disk - providing MESSENGER will do this. As I've just got into this Micronet lark, more bits of jargon have appeared. What is "scrolling software" and what is it used for? Could someone tell us all about the various types of code files that seem to be in use.What uses what and why? By this I mean text, data, open-type, ASCII, array, etc. If I do a CAT*1 on the Opus in the vicinity of Masterfile I get file types of for Basic and for Code- I suppose f$() might be Data but what is

? I found out by accident that Tasword 2 text files LOAD at 32000 on the Spectrum (and 97536 on the SAM?) but never seen this in writing. Sometimes there are queries about the ROM in the Opus Discovery regarding disassembly, etc. As Paul Cheffings has produced a new version of the ROM (EXCOM) no doubt he could supply all ROM details required. Ring him on 0507 - 328794. I've just had several 'verify failed' messages- can't find an edge connector to clean, what next? Just copied "Tasword" onto this disc in Drive 2. Then went to LOAD this file from it- it went back to Drive 1! Charlie Kingwell Brian Cavers to Charlie Kingwell Yes, CATLOADER is one of several of our programs that, if we had put it in a glossy package and charged `9.99 both Spectrum and SAM users would have been there queuing at the door!Give it away in OUTLET and many do not really appreciate what they've got.That said, I must admit that it needs updating - especially for use with Masterdos and I have a lot of notes for improvements. What I don't have is time - as usual! Brian Gaff's AUTOMENU(OUTLET 34) will check and verify all tracks and sectors on a SAM disc or SEEK 'N PEEK(OUTLET 45) will display and edit sectors. Regarding SAM SUPPLEMENT's own program to read an Opus disc I can only recommend you write to them! After all, the original author of the program should be able to help better than I. The error appears to be that it is trying to print the name of the Opus disc from the CAT sector in DISC$ but it contains a code of between 16 to 21(PAPER,INK,etc.) followed by a value that is too high (e.g., INK 99!). This could mean you named the disc with a funny name (e.g. CHR$ 17+CHR$ 99 +"TEE HEE!") but is more likely that the program is looking at the wrong sector or the wrong part of the sector. The drive number should not matter but, as I say, I'm sure SAM SUPPLEMENT will try to help. MICRONET has VIEWDATA pages that are screens displayed one at a time then cleared and the next screen displayed. Many (most?) other bulletin boards display text but when the screen is full and more text is added the early text is just scrolled up off the top of the screen just as when you keep using a BASIC PRINT statement on SAM or Spectrum. It needs special software to access these bulletin boards called "Scrolling software". DR.SCROLL,`5-from B.G. SERVICES, 64 Roebuck Road, Chessington, Surrey, KT9 1JX works with the VTX5000 to let you access these "scrolling boards". B.G. also do a `1 PD tape with bits including scrolling software. 'P' in a CAT display is probably a 'PRINT' or 'OPEN-TYPE' file (these are synonymous terms). It can be "written" or PRINTed to just like printing to the screen or a printer and "read" with the use of INPUT or INKEY$. Consult your Opus or Masterdos manual! A text file is not a special disc file but any file (BASIC, CODE, OPEN-TYPE) containing text and, perhaps, print codes.ASCII files are virtually synonymous. In the case of Tasword 2 it is CODE but on many computers, OPEN-TYPE files are more commonly used for text. Likewise 'data' could be any values in BASIC or CODE etc. used by a program. However, on SAM and Spectrum, DATA files are BASIC arrays which have been saved (again, see your manual!). The "VERIFY FAILED" message I assume is in Tasword 2 on the SAM, yes? If so, it is almost certain that you are using an early version of MASTERDOS that has a bug. Apply for an upgrade or remove the VERIFY command from the BASIC in Tasword. Wait until it crashes again then note down the line number.We had this in OUTLET recently but I forget the line number. As for Tasword reverting to Drive 1, remove your disc, try again, wait a few seconds for it to crash, note the line number and adjust the load command. Why not add an INPUT? For example, INPUT "Enter drive No.";DN$ then make the load command... LOAD "D"+DN$+":"+N$. The 'N$' at the end must be whatever string name is used in your Tasword already.I think the version you have uses A$ and if you can see DEVICE D1 in lines 2020 and 2040 then remove them instead of the foregoing and you should then find you will access the "current drive". If you want to be able to change the drive number though,try the preceding. Ah, yes, I think the VERIFY in your version is at the end of line 1040. Just press B at the main Tasword menu to enter BASIC and after making the changes enter RS to resave the program. Hope that helps. ```text - Brian. ``` From: Chris Oliver, STAFFS Dear Brian & Ron, Enclosed is my contribution to the OUTLET `5000 fund with fervent wishes that you are able to keep on producing the superb mag. for many more than just another 12 months. To add my views to recent comments on the amount of Sam space:- Yes, it is a little disappointing that the content is no longer totally for the 48K machines but there are so many other good bits in every issue that you shouldn't consider this a real complaint. I often wonder though, what musical treats the 128ers get that we don't? Talking of music: an IBM- compatible has infiltrated our household(purely for educational purposes,of course) but who said they're not games machines? If you can, look at a game called "Wing Commander". To appreciate it fully you'll need a midi interface to a stereo sound system. It's compressed on five discs so you will also need two megabytes to expand into. The involvement is so great that it feels natural between missions to go into the on-screen bar, have a chat to the barman and relax by playing a video-game version of "Wing Commander". I can't remember who it was in the 1960s who couldn't envisage home computers needing any more than 1k of RAM? It's encouraging to see from the letters that you are getting new readers, but I suppose they've all got Super SAMS? Congratulations on the continu- ing high standards of OUTLET and best wishes for the future. Cheers, Chris Oliver Thanks Chris. For anyone who may be wondering what the `5000 fund is - it was just a joke about us ruefully pondering the amount of payments we've paid out over the years for all the programs contributed to OUTLET! ```text - Brian. ```

## Letters (1) Октябрь 1991 г. | Страница | Ответ --- | --- | --- Как нам написать... | 02 | - Ted Payne | 03 | 07 Billy Humphries | 08 | 10 Brian Cooper | 13 | 15 John Hall | 16 | 17 John White | 19 | 22 Charlie Kingwell | 23 | 28 Chris Oliver | 34 | 36 **ПОЖАЛУЙСТА, ПРИСЫЛАЙТЕ ВАШИ ТЕКСТОВЫЕ ФАЙЛЫ!** Текст принимается в любом виде для рубрики OUTLETTERS: файлы текстовых процессоров (указывайте каких), напечатанные или написанные от руки письма. Однако, пожалуйста, по возможности присылайте текстовый файл, чтобы ваше письмо не пришлось набирать заново! Нам проще всего редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32, но мы будем рады текстовому файлу в ЛЮБОМ формате! Пожалуйста, укажите, если есть части вашего письма, которые вы не хотели бы публиковать, но мы в любом случае руководствуемся своим усмотрением. Письма также могут быть отредактированы для ясности и сокращения... Пожалуйста, укажите, приветствуете ли вы прямую переписку с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес. --- **От: Ted Payne, SOUTHPORT** Дорогие Рон и Брайан, Мое оборудование теперь выглядит так: Spectrum +3, Multiface 3 и Star LC10, подключенные к портативному 14-дюймовому цветному телевизору Samsung. До того как я приобрел принтер, я с интересом читал письма в OUTLET и в некоторых бумажных журналах о множестве разнообразных проблем, с которыми сталкиваются люди, пытаясь заставить разные вещи работать вместе. Однако, если только мой конкретный +3 не уникален (в чем я сомневаюсь), я не понимаю, в чем проблема, потому что для всего в OUTLET, что я хочу распечатать, я просто нажимаю нужную клавишу (или клавиши), и принтер Star оживает, выдавая идеальную твердую копию. Даже Tasword 2 (дисковая версия, которую вы опубликовали некоторое время назад) печатает идеально, что подтверждает распечатка этого письма. Я прочитал пару писем от людей, которые, по-видимому, испытывают трудности с подачей сигнала со Spectrum на видеомагнитофон. Главная проблема, с которой я столкнулся при попытке это сделать, заключается в том, что частота, используемая для передачи сигнала с видеомагнитофона на телевизор, почти совпадает с частотой сигнала Spectrum. Если вы используете T-образный антенный разветвитель на задней панели телевизора и подключаете к нему и видеомагнитофон, и Speccy, изображение с обоих устройств будет искаженным. Решение состоит в том, чтобы подключить T-разветвитель в антенный вход (IN) видеомагнитофона, а затем подключить к нему кабели от Speccy и антенны. Если на вашем видеомагнитофоне есть тестовый режим (обычно переключатель на задней панели), выберите его. Найдите небольшое отверстие на задней панели видеомагнитофона, через которое видна головка регулировочного винта. Иногда она помечена как UHF или цифрами, например, 38-62. Поверните этот винт влево или вправо примерно на четверть оборота. Все, что вы делаете, — это настраиваете частоту сигнала, передаваемого с видеомагнитофона на телевизор. Затем перенастройте канал видеомагнитофона на телевизоре, пока не получите картинку с видеомагнитофона. Как только изображение с видеомагнитофона появится на телевизоре, останется только выключить тестовый режим (если он был) и настроить свободный канал на видеомагнитофоне, пока не увидите экран Speccy. Вуаля! Теперь вы можете записывать все, что делаете на Speccy, для многочасовых повторов, или записывать любимые моменты из OUTLET, чтобы смотреть их, даже если Speccy нет дома. Кстати, можете ли вы порекомендовать хорошую, простую в использовании и недорогую программу для настольных издательских систем (DTP) для +3? Спасибо за труд по созданию такого замечательного журнала, С наилучшими пожеланиями, Ted Payne **Brian Cavers — Ted Payne** Спасибо, Тед. На самом деле существует только одна программа для настольных издательских систем для Spectrum: P.C.G.'s DTP PACK. Это три программы: WORDMASTER (текстовый процессор) — £13.95, HEADLINER (дизайнер графики/заголовков) — £10.95 и TYPELINER (собственно издательская система) — £18.95. Все три программы интегрированы, поэтому основная программа легко обращается к остальным с диска. Полный комплект стоит £37.95. Эти цены указаны для кассет или дисков Disciple/+D. Добавьте £2 за дисковую версию для +3. Пишите: P.C.G., 61 School Street, Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW (Тел: 0229 836957). — Брайан --- **От: Billy Humphries** Во-первых, я хотел бы сказать, как сильно мне нравится ваш журнал — вы вкладываете так много сил каждый месяц. Мне нужна информация по принтерам. У меня есть Spectrum 128 (черный), 48+ и DISCIPLE. Я хочу купить 24-игольчатый цветной принтер для печати скриншотов, листингов программ и копий списков видеокассет и т. д. Я покупаю OUTLET на кассете и копирую его на дисковод с помощью RUN 9982. Я хотел бы копировать текстовые файлы, но пока единственный успех был, когда я копирую загрузчик текста (любой), нажимаю BREAK при приглашении "play tape" и загружаю код текстового файла с диска, который был сохранен с помощью "Oli's Readr" (OUTLET 14), чтобы найти адрес и длину, и копирую код через `LOAD "NAME" CODE ADD,LEN`. Есть ли способ лучше и аккуратнее? Вы могли бы подсказать быстрый способ загрузки всех текстовых файлов с одного диска, а затем можно было бы использовать программу типа PROMPT: загрузить код с кассеты (y/n?), сохранить код на диск, распечатать на принтере, загрузить следующий файл с кассеты/диска. С нетерпением жду следующего выпуска и надеюсь, что вы сможете помочь с принтером. Спасибо, Billy Humphries **Brian Cavers — Billy Humphries** Я бы выбрал Citizen Swift 24, у которого есть опциональный "цветной комплект". Он стоит от £300 до £400, но на вашем месте я бы поискал лучшие цены и постарался попасть на демонстрацию в магазине. Я приводил немного информации о нем в ответе Norman Haigh в OUTLETTERS 45, а полный обзор Майка Пайка был в выпуске 48, если у вас есть этот номер. Однако замечу, что я лично не пользовался этой машиной, но на бумаге она выглядит отлично и получила хорошие отзывы. Рекомендую попробовать PBT. Они продают SWIFT 24 всего за £295.50 + £5 за пересылку, и у них также можно купить цветные ленты за £14.99. PBT находятся по адресу: Port Talbot Workshops, Unit 17, Addison Road, Port Talbot, SA12 6HZ. Тел: 0639 885008. Они также занимаются ремонтом +D и Disciple, так что хорошо знакомы со Spectrum. Я могу их рекомендовать. Кстати, для получения цветных скриншотов вам понадобится специальное программное обеспечение. Если будете связываться с PBT, можете спросить их об этом. Я знаю, что у них есть софт для цветной печати, но он может быть только для 9-игольчатых принтеров или только для SAM. Сейчас не вспомню. Кажется, это программа Даррена Тэлбота, которая была у нас в OUTBOARD некоторое время назад. Извините, не могу сейчас точно сказать, а память у меня как (как называют те штуки, что полны дырок?). Что касается переноса файлов OUTLET с кассеты на диски +D, проще всего использовать UNITRANS+ (OUTLET 20). Это отличная программа, которая делает все полностью автоматически. Однако заметьте, что она не меняет код BASIC, поэтому любой, который загружает другие файлы, потребует изменения синтаксиса и т. д. Теперь, когда вы увидели наши новые цены, уверен, вы поняли, что нет смысла брать кассетную версию, если у вас есть +D, так как цена одна и та же! — Брайан --- **От: Brian Cooper** Дорогие Рон и Брайан, Спасибо за очередной супер-выпуск 'Outlet'. Интересно, сможете ли вы помочь мне со следующей проблемой, возникшей с отличной программой 'Card Index' (OUTLET 48) от Стюарта Редферна и его папы! (С программой все в порядке, просто не хватает моих знаний). Я не могу заставить свой принтер CPA.80+ делать перевод строки при распечатке информации с индексной карточки. Стюарт и его папа советуют изменить строку 7000, но, как я уже сказал, мои знания в программировании довольно ограничены. Строка выглядит так: ```text 7000 POKE @VAL"6",NOT PI: RETURN ``` Большое спасибо за помощь и продолжайте в том же духе! — Brian Cooper P.S. Не могли бы вы передать мою благодарность человеку из Уилтшира, который очень любезно ответил на мою просьбу о руководстве к 'TLW'. Я не знаю вашего имени или адреса, но спасибо. Спасибо также другим фанатам Spectrum, которые предложили помощь! **Brian Cavers — Brian Cooper** Да, ответ заключается в изменении строки 355 следующим образом: сделайте LIST строки и вставьте апостроф между словом LPRINT и m$(n) ближе к концу строки, изменив таким образом... LPRINT m$(n) на LPRINT'm$(n). Апостроф в языке BASIC в операторе PRINT или LPRINT (не внутри кавычек) вызывает перевод строки, так что LPRINT''''' сделает 5 переводов строк. Кстати, добавление `POKE @6,1:LPRINT CHR$27;"W";CHR$1:` в начало строки 7000 даст широкую печать. Пользователи +3 должны заменить POKE @6,1 на FORMAT LPRINT "U". В Microdrive и Opus используйте OPEN #3;"B": — Брайан --- **От: John Hall, BOURNEMOUTH** Я получаю OUTLET на 3.5" дисках для использования с системой Plus D, и все хорошо, пока вы не помещаете на диск программы, такие как German Folk Song. Мой Plus D используется со Spectrum +3, который, конечно, я не могу использовать в режиме 128K. Могу ли я конвертировать программу с диска для работы в режиме 128K или мне нужно заказывать диск для Plus 3? Я очень ценю качество и разнообразие программ, которые я получил до сих пор. Были ли на ваших ранних дисках какие-нибудь программы с фракталами? John Hall **Brian Cavers — John Hall** Мне сказали, что нельзя попасть в редактор 128K BASIC, если Plus D подключен к +3, поэтому загрузите программу с Plus D, нажмите BREAK и введите: ```text 8917 IF K$="S" THEN GO TO 9972 ``` RUN 9983, чтобы сохранить на кассету. Сбросьте (reset) для входа в меню загрузчика 128K и перезагрузите с кассеты, нажав ENTER без диска в дисководе +3, и все должно работать. Вы можете попробовать сделать снимок (snapshot) 48K или 128K на диск +D, или если вы нажмете "S" на титульной странице, он должен сохраниться на диск +3 и должен перезагрузиться как загрузочный файл из меню. Я, конечно, не могу все это протестировать! Есть отличная фрактальная программа от Криса и Пола Оливеров в OUTLET 35 под названием BROT. Spectrum, очевидно, не может конкурировать с графикой и скоростью обработки Amiga, но BROT, тем не менее, способен создавать неплохие изображения Мандельброта. Другие интересные программы с фракталами — TRI2 (OUTLET 34) и FRAX (OUTLET 16). Еще одна программа, которая может вам понравиться, где нужно вводить значения для создания отличных 3D-изображений (но которая НЕ является фрактальным генератором), — это ISOMETRIC (OUTLET 26). Я считаю, что это потрясающая программа. — Брайан --- **От: John White, LEICESTER** Дорогие Рон и Брайан, Спасибо за еще один качественный OUTLET (выпуск 048). Ссылаясь на письмо Джона Кауча о печати знака "`" на Citizen 120-D+ и ответ Брайана: я раньше настраивал свой 120-D на английские символы, когда использовал Tasword 2, но теперь сбросил настройки на "#=#" и изменил коды принтера в T2, чтобы назначить те, что привел Брайан, на клавишу 8 в графическом режиме. Теперь я могу использовать английские символы, если мне нужен ` в тексте. Сказав это, я теперь обычно использую Tasword 3, и если Джон Кауч (или другие) тоже его используют, то для них должно быть возможным печатать `###### до потери сознания! Не знаю, что есть в D+, чего нет в моем D, но мой метод таков: 1. Зайдите в меню TW3 и выберите C для настройки программы. 2. Продолжайте нажимать ENTER до пункта "define normal print chars". 3. Ответьте Y и следуйте подсказкам. Введите "`" и введите 27 94 156, затем снова ENTER для выхода из последовательности. 4. Если клавиши для выбора режимов IBM и Epson не были определены, то: 5. Ответьте Y на "define printer control chars" и нажмите пробел для остальных 16 символов. 6. Выберите клавишу для режима IBM и введите 27 126 53 49. 7. Выберите клавишу для режима Epson и введите 27 126 53 48. 8. Нажмите ENTER, когда закончите, и удерживайте, пока не вернется меню. 9. MICRONET имеет страницы VIEWDATA — это экраны, которые отображаются по одному, затем очищаются, и отображается следующий экран. Многие (большинство?) другие доски объявлений отображают текст, но когда экран заполняется и добавляется новый текст, старый просто прокручивается вверх и исчезает с экрана, точно так же, как если бы вы постоянно использовали оператор BASIC PRINT на SAM или Spectrum. Для доступа к этим доскам объявлений требуется специальное программное обеспечение, называемое «Scrolling software». DR.SCROLL, `5 от B.G. SERVICES, 64 Roebuck Road, Chessington, Surrey, KT9 1JX работает с VTX5000, позволяя вам получать доступ к этим «прокручиваемым доскам». B.G. также выпускают PD-кассету за `1 с различными вещами, включая «scrolling software». «P» в отображении CAT — это, вероятно, файл «PRINT» или «OPEN-TYPE» (это синонимы). В него можно «писать» (PRINT) точно так же, как при выводе на экран или принтер, и «читать» с помощью INPUT или INKEY$. Обратитесь к руководству по Opus или Masterdos! Текстовый файл — это не особый дисковый файл, а любой файл (BASIC, CODE, OPEN-TYPE), содержащий текст и, возможно, коды печати. Файлы ASCII практически синонимичны. В случае с Tasword 2 это CODE, но на многих компьютерах файлы OPEN-TYPE чаще используются для текста. Точно так же «data» может быть любыми значениями в BASIC, CODE и т.д., используемыми программой. Однако на SAM и Spectrum файлы DATA — это массивы BASIC, которые были сохранены (опять же, смотрите ваше руководство!). Сообщение «VERIFY FAILED», я полагаю, появляется в Tasword 2 на SAM, верно? Если так, то почти наверняка вы используете раннюю версию MASTERDOS, в которой есть ошибка. Подайте заявку на обновление или удалите команду VERIFY из BASIC в Tasword.
